title: Latency-Aware Throttle & Routing Playbook for Safe Batch/Cache Optimizations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and implementation for applying cost-optimization recommendations (batching and KV-prefetch/cache profiles) with strong latency and throughput SLO guardrails. The goal is to let Optimize recommend aggressive config deltas while the runtime enforces per-cohort limiters, SLO-aware routing, and early anomaly detection so customer-facing latency/throughput is preserved and rollbacks are automatic when risk thresholds are crossed.
motivation: We already have automated batching/cache recommendation signals but lack a deterministic, observable path to apply them safely at scale. This work reduces manual ops overhead, lowers unit cost, and prevents regressions to 99th percentile latency and customer throughput during optimization runs.
design_decisions: Limiter hierarchy: cohort-level & global soft-limit + hard-failover. Soft-limits trigger probational routing; hard limits trigger immediate rollback to previous stable profile.
SLO-aware routing: route a fraction of traffic to optimized profile only when rolling averages of p50/p95 are within threshold; otherwise route to stable variant.
Anomaly windows: use both short window (30s) and medium window (5m) detectors to catch burst and persistent regressions.
Telemetry gating: require both latency telemetry and throughput success-rate signals before promoting any config change beyond shadow mode.
Config application model: staged apply (shadow -> canary cohort -> graduated) with automatic backoff and enforced cool-down between steps.
Observability-first rollout: every apply must create a dashboard snapshot with token-level cost delta, latency histograms, and cohort traffic split view.

Decisions to delay: full per-request adaptive batching (on-the-fly micro-batching) is out of scope for this ticket; we'll rely on precomputed batching profiles generated by Optimize and applied via this playbook.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Shadow apply for 0% real traffic for 1 hour; record latent metrics and compare generated outputs to baseline for quality regression.
Step 1: Canary cohort = 1% of traffic for 15 minutes; SLO gates: p95 latency delta <= +15ms and throughput >= 99% of baseline; anomaly detectors monitor both short (30s) and medium (5m) windows.
Step 2: If Step 1 passes, expand to 10% for 30 minutes with same SLO gates tightened to +10ms on p95.
Step 3: Expand to 40% for 60 minutes with continuous monitoring and staged increases only when rolling averages are stable.
Step 4: Full graduation with automated cleanup of shadow rules and promotion of profile to stable config repository.
Step Failure: On any hard-alert (defined in Monitoring) immediately stop acceptance, shift routing away from optimized profile, and mark profile as failed. Begin a forensic runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook documentation published to Confluence with diagrams, run commands, and rollback steps.
Runtime implements cohort soft/hard limiters and SLO-aware routing flags behind a feature gate with config API.
Automated canary pipeline executes staged apply and honors cool-down; a sample canary successfully completes without SLO breach in lab tests.
Anomaly detectors (30s and 5m) integrated with alerting and automatic routing switch-over.
Dashboards are generated automatically for every applied profile and persist for at least 7 days.
E2E test that simulates a problematic workload triggers auto-rollback in the canary stage.
testing_plan: Unit tests for limiter logic, including edge cases where request sizes spike and KV cache miss rates increase.
Integration test in staging: run Optimize profile apply in shadow and assert no traffic is impacted and no alerts fire.
Chaos test: synthetic latency pump applied to backend GPUs during a canary run; ensure system reroutes and rolls back within SLO-defined window.
Load test: 10k qps simulated traffic across cohorts measuring p50/p95/p99 and throughput before/after optimization profile.
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary SLOs to monitor: token-generation p95 latency (ms), success throughput (tokens/s), 5xx rate, and tail error budget consumption.
Short-window detector: 30s rolling alarm if p95 > baseline + 15ms or throughput < 98% of baseline.
Medium-window detector: 5m rolling alarm if p95 > baseline + 10ms or throughput < 99% of baseline.
Hard-failure trigger: sustained 5m breach of P95 by >25ms OR 5xx rate increase >3x baseline triggers immediate traffic switch to stable profile.
Alert channels: #infra-alerts (pager), SRE on-call rotation, and an automated ticket opened in Linear if rollback occurs.
Dashboard widgets: cohort traffic split, latency histograms, cost delta per token, cache hit/miss ratio, and KV prefetch queue depth.
Instrumentation: tag all telemetry with profile_id, cohort_id, rollout_step for filtering in dashboards and automated rules.
rollback_plan: Two-tier rollback: soft rollback (traffic shift) executed automatically by routing policy on soft-limit breach; full config revert (hard rollback) executed when hard-failure trigger fires or after operator approval. Forensic artifacts (profile_id, timestamps, logs, heap snapshots) are archived to the opt-rollback S3 bucket and linked in the generated Linear incident. Automatic revert must complete within 90s of hard trigger. Post-rollback runbook must include root-cause hypothesis and candidate mitigations.

progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Optimize teams. Agreed on feature-gate approach and cohort model. Action: runtime to prototype limiter primitives.
2026-02-20: Prototype limiter implemented in sandbox runtime; basic soft/hard behavior validated with microbench harness. PR opened: https://github.com/redwoodinference/runtime/pull/478
2026-02-28: Design review with PM and Design; UX requested explicit rollback CTA in Console and a visible cooldown timer for canaries. Added ticket ENG-40327 for Console changes.

2026-03-04: Anomaly detector PoC completed using short and medium rolling windows backed by SignalProc service. False positives observed with GC pauses; SRE suggested excluding GC-marked spans. Added mitigation to detector tuning.
2026-03-09: Staging run of shadow apply completed for 2 recommended profiles. No SLO regressions. Preparing canary runs next week.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: focus on limiter failure semantics, rollback latency guarantees, and alert thresholds. Pay special attention to instrumentation tags and dashboard snapshot retention policy. Make sure the planned automatic revert timeframe (90s) is achievable operationally.
